beats.text: Five Stoic lessons for making peace with the one certainty we all avoid.
One. Memento mori — remember you will die. Not to depress you, but to wake you up.
Two. You felt no fear in the endless time before your birth. The time after is no different.
Three. Treat every goodbye as practice. Love people as things briefly lent, never owned.
Four. A life isn't measured by its length, said Seneca, but by how fully it was lived.
Five. Live each day as if it could be the last — not in panic, but in care for what matters.
Death is the teacher, said the Stoics, that makes every ordinary day suddenly worth something.
